Fok-Paap tests of multinomial logit misspecification

Source: R/iia.R
fp_tests.Rd

The two tests of Fok and Paap (2025), built on the property that under the multinomial logit the choice between any two alternatives \(j, m\), given that one of them is chosen, is a binary logit in the utility difference \(V_j - V_m\). Pairs are the \(J - 1\) base pairs or all \(J(J-1)/2\) pairs.

Usage

fp_tests(
  object,
  pairs = c("all", "base"),
  tests = c("cl", "gmm"),
  gmm = c("two-step", "iterated", "projected"),
  vcov = c("joint", "difference"),
  maxit = 50L
)

Arguments

object

A fitted mnl() model with at least three alternatives. A fit with diverging coefficients (separation) draws a warning. Along a diverging direction neither estimator has an estimate, so \(Q_1\) leaves those directions out: the composite-likelihood estimator keeps the fit's values along them, the two estimators are compared on the other directions, and the degrees of freedom are reduced by their number (attr(, "details")$q1_left_out names the coefficients that move along them and $q1_left_out_rank counts the directions; a separated reference cell is one direction through an intercept and a dummy, whose sum stays in the comparison). The statistic then does not depend on where the optimizer stopped. \(Q_2\) is not computed (NA): its moment conditions have no finite solution along a diverging direction, and the moments at the point where the optimizer stopped depend on that point. In boot_pvalue() a replicate that separates has fewer degrees of freedom than the observed statistic it is compared with.

pairs

"all" (default) or "base".

tests

Which tests to compute: "cl", "gmm", or both (default).

gmm

"two-step" (default), "iterated", or "projected"; see Details.

vcov

The covariance in \(Q_1\): "joint" (default) or "difference"; see Details.

maxit

Maximum number of weight-matrix updates for gmm = "iterated".

Value

A data frame of class "iia_test" with one row per test: test, statistic, df, p.value, psd, and pairs. The attribute "details" holds the CL and GMM estimates and the reciprocal condition number of the moment covariance; on a separated fit also q1_left_out and q1_left_out_rank, and theta_cl then equals the fit along the directions left out, where vcov_cl has no variance.

Details

Composite-likelihood Hausman test (Q1). The pairwise composite likelihood estimator \(\hat\theta_{CL}\) maximizes the sum over pairs and cases of the binary logit log-likelihoods; its covariance is the Godambe sandwich. Under correct specification the MLE and the CL estimator are both consistent and only the MLE is efficient, so \(Q_1 = (\hat\theta_{ML} - \hat\theta_{CL})'(V_{CL} - V_{ML})^{-1}(\hat\theta_{ML} - \hat\theta_{CL})\) is chi-square on \(\dim\theta\) degrees of freedom (F&P eq. 18). Under the multinomial logit the composite-likelihood estimator is nearly efficient (its variance is within a few percent of the MLE's in most directions), so \(V_{CL} - V_{ML}\) is a small difference of two separately estimated matrices, and the sampling noise of the sandwich makes it indefinite in nearly every sample: in the package's simulations (verification/ in the development repository) it was never positive semi-definite, 44 percent of the statistics were negative, and the rejection rates were 0.033, 0.042, and 0.049 at the 1, 5, and 10 percent levels. The default vcov = "joint" therefore estimates the covariance of \(\hat\theta_{ML} - \hat\theta_{CL}\) directly, from the stacked influence functions \(V_{ML} s^{ML}_i - H_{CL}^{-1} s^{CL}_i\) of the two estimators (summed by cluster when the fit has a cluster), as the joint form of hausman_mcfadden() does; it is positive semi-definite by construction and its rejection rates in the same simulations were 0.015, 0.062, and 0.112. vcov = "difference" is the formula of F&P eq. 18, for comparison with published values; psd reports whether its covariance difference was positive semi-definite, and the p-value refers max(statistic, 0) to the chi-square (a negative statistic is no evidence against the model).

GMM overidentification test (Q2). With moment conditions \(E[(1\{y = j\} - \Lambda(V_j - V_m))\, 1\{y \in \{j, m\}\}\, \zeta] = 0\) for every pair, instruments \(\zeta = (x, w_j - w_m)\), the parameters are overidentified and Hansen's J statistic at the efficient GMM estimate is chi-square on (number of moments \(-\) number of parameters) degrees of freedom (F&P eq. 19). gmm = "two-step" (default) is Hansen's two-step estimator: the weight matrix is the inverse empirical covariance of the moments at the MLE (F&P eq. 15), the parameters are re-estimated under it, and the statistic is evaluated at that estimate with its own weight matrix. gmm = "iterated" repeats the update until the estimate stops moving, as Fok and Paap do; with many moments relative to the sample the iteration can fail to settle (a warning is issued and the last iterate is used), which is why it is not the default. gmm = "projected" evaluates the moments at the MLE and projects out the estimated directions (Newey's conditional-moment / C form), which has the same asymptotic distribution without a GMM optimization. All three have the same degrees of freedom. With case-specific covariates only, the overidentifying restrictions carry information only through the covariates (Fok and Paap 2025, Section 2.2): with few or weak covariates the moment covariance is near singular and the test has little power; its reciprocal condition number is reported. Where the moments are linearly dependent (one binary covariate, say) the moment covariance is singular: the statistic is then computed on its generalized inverse, its degrees of freedom are the rank of the moment covariance minus the number of parameters, and a warning says so.

Units of the covariates. Where they are computed, neither statistic depends on the units of the covariates, on their centering, or on a factor's reference level. The instruments of \(Q_2\) are put on a canonical scale before the moments are formed, and the contrast of \(Q_1\) is whitened by the covariance of the maximum-likelihood estimator, so that the directions a generalized inverse drops are the same in any parametrization.

When the tests are not computed. Both tests compare estimators at the fit. Where the fit's information matrix is ill-conditioned on the directions compared (reciprocal condition number of its normalized form below 1e-9, the rule of the fit's ill_conditioned flag), the estimates are determined to few digits along some direction and the statistics would depend on where the optimizer stopped: both are NA, with a warning. That condition number does not depend on the covariates' units, but a covariate far from its origin (a calendar year) is nearly collinear with the constant and can bring it below the bound; centering it helps. \(Q_1\) is also NA when the composite-likelihood estimator does not exist (its sensitivity matrix is singular).

References

Fok, D. and Paap, R. (2025). New misspecification tests for multinomial logit models. Journal of Choice Modelling, 54, 100531. doi:10.1016/j.jocm.2024.100531

Varin, C., Reid, N. and Firth, D. (2011). An overview of composite likelihood methods. Statistica Sinica, 21, 5-42.

Hansen, L.P. (1982). Large sample properties of generalized method of moments estimators. Econometrica, 50, 1029-1054. doi:10.2307/1912775

See also

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- rmnl(1500, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5), d = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.9)))
m <- mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d)
fp_tests(m)
#> Fok-Paap (2025) misspecification tests, all pairs 
#>                                            test statistic df p.value  psd pairs
#>                 Fok-Paap CL Hausman (Q1, joint)     8.593  9   0.476 TRUE   all
#>  Fok-Paap GMM overidentification (Q2, two-step)    18.101  9   0.034   NA   all
fp_tests(m, gmm = "projected")
#> Fok-Paap (2025) misspecification tests, all pairs 
#>                                             test statistic df p.value  psd
#>                  Fok-Paap CL Hausman (Q1, joint)     8.593  9  0.4757 TRUE
#>  Fok-Paap GMM overidentification (Q2, projected)    15.346  9  0.0819   NA
#>  pairs
#>    all
#>    all
fp_tests(m, gmm = "iterated")
#> Warning: The iterated GMM estimator did not settle within 50 weight-matrix updates; the last iterate is used. Consider gmm = "two-step" or "projected".
#> Fok-Paap (2025) misspecification tests, all pairs 
#>                                            test statistic df p.value  psd pairs
#>                 Fok-Paap CL Hausman (Q1, joint)     8.593  9  0.4757 TRUE   all
#>  Fok-Paap GMM overidentification (Q2, iterated)    19.204  9  0.0235   NA   all
